The OTIF score that hid the real problem

A stable headline service measure can coexist with growing expediting, repeated promise changes and avoidable management effort.

Illustrative scenario analysis · 6–8 minute read
This article illustrates a recurring supply-chain pattern and the JourneyIQ Supply Chain Diagnostic method. It does not describe a named client, completed engagement or verified customer outcome.

The situation

A stable aggregate can hide repeated promise changes, partial deliveries and the manual intervention required to produce an acceptable final result.

What the headline misses

A line that arrives on time after five chasers and an emergency replan scores like a line that flowed without intervention. The customer sees the same receipt; the organisation pays a different cost.

How the diagnostic reframes it

Reconstruct the sequence from requirement to commitment, change, shipment, receipt and exception handling. Keep observed events, calculated patterns and assumed operating cost separate.

The management decision

Use the evidence to decide whether action belongs in supplier recovery, commitment rules, planning parameters, escalation thresholds or the service definition itself.
